newsitem.title: USA: Campbell in deal on retiree medical costs.
newsitem.headline: Campbell in deal on retiree medical costs.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co said it had reached a tentative $114.5 million settlement with a group of retired employees who sued the company after it cut their medical benefits in 1992.

Under the settlement, which must be approved by a federal court judge in Camden, New Jersey, Campbell will pay the $114.5 million to help cover medical costs for the group of 12,000 retirees and their dependents, Campbell spokesman Kevin Lowery said.
Lowery said the settlement, if approved, would not affect current earnings because the cost had been reserved previously.

He said the court had earlier ruled Campbell had the right to cut the benefits, but the case has remained open to consider whether Campbell had properly communicated to its retired employees the cut in benefits.

Describing the settlement, Lowery said, "We went to the other side, and working together with them, we made a proposal that said we would be willing to put money into a fund that would essentially provide lifetime medical benefits."

The fund will provide managed-care coverage, including up to 80 percent of drug costs, through health maintenance organizations. Retirees who wished to continue in the federal Medicare program also would receive prescription drug benefits and reimbursements for 80 percent of prescription costs.
The agreement includes a $3.5 million hardship fund for special cases, and provides reimbursement for certain costs borne by the retiree group since 1992, Lowery said.
U.S. District Court Judge Stanley Brotman is to hold a hearing on the plan on January 10. Lowery said former employees eligible for the propsed settlement were notified of the deal by mail last week.
The proposal does not affect Campbell employees who retired after the cut in benefits was announced.
